answer_1.quote: Neural dialogue generation has drawn increasing attention due to its vast commercial values and practical demands.

answer_2.quote: We conducted both automatic and human evaluation to compare the performance of the models... We employ two kinds of automatic metrics to evaluate all models. The reference-based metrics, perplexity (PPL), BLEU (%), and the embedding metrics (including embedding average (AVE), embedding greedy (GRE), embedding extrema (EXT)) , and coherence (COH)... The count-based metrics, distinct (Dist-{1,2,3} (%)) and KL divergence...

answer_4.quote: We conducted human evaluation to assess the quality of response. We randomly selected 200 test examples from each dataset and asked three annotators to judge which generated response in each pair (RegDG and baseline) is better (i.e., win, lose or tie) in terms of Diversity (how much the generated response contains meaningful information), Relevance (how likely the generated response is coherent to both dialogue history and future conversation), and Fluency (how likely the generated response is from human).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators judge which response is better (win/lose/tie) for Diversity, Relevance, and Fluency.
